rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests the impact of multimodal integration (RNA + image) with specific encoders (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l), transformer aggregation, and concat fusion. It isolates the effect of multimodal design choices while using well-established components, balancing exploration of key factors (multimodal vs. rna_only) and providing a baseline for further comparisons.

Existing evidence shows config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieves 0.5988 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from transformer to avgpool (while keeping other parameters identical) improves performance, isolating the impact of aggregation method. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether transformer or avgpool is better for this task, balancing exploration of key design choices with minimal parameter changes.

The existing evidence shows that config_004 (multimodal, scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 while keeping other components (scgpt RNA, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) consistent, isolating the impact of image encoder choice. This clarifies whether resnet50 improves performance over imagenet_vit_l in a multiprofile multimodal setup, balancing exploration of critical design choices with exploitation of the current top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (config_020), keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion identical. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, while building on the successful multimodal/multiprofile framework. It balances exploitation (using proven components) with exploration (testing a key variable) to determine if scgpt outperforms pca_n2000 in this context.

Existing evidence shows config_004 (multimodal) achieves 0.5988 accuracy, while rna-only models like config_013 (0.5176) and config_010 (0.4710) perform worse. This experiment tests whether removing image data (rna_only) while keeping the high-performing RNA encoder (scgpt) and aggregation (transformer) from config_004 improves accuracy. It isolates the impact of multimodal fusion versus RNA-only features, addressing uncertainty about whether image data contributes meaningfully.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scgpt RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and transformer aggregation (like config_004) achieve the highest accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It builds on the strong foundation of config_004 while exploring a critical design choice with minimal other changes.

Existing evidence shows config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) has the highest accuracy. Uncertainty remains about whether the RNA encoder (scgpt vs scvi_n200) or fusion method (concat vs weighted) is more impactful. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA with the same image encoder and aggregation as config_004 but changes fusion to weighted, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder while maintaining most other parameters.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, weighted fusion, and transformer aggregation (config_031) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method from transformer to avgpool (config_051) affects performance, clarifying the importance of aggregation strategy. It isolates this key design choice while keeping other components aligned with the current top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder combinations (config_051) achieve 0.6776 accuracy, while transformer aggregation (config_031) with imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieves 0.7249. This experiment tests whether using transformer aggregation with resnet50 image encoder (config_025) can bridge the performance gap, clarifying the interaction between aggregation method and image encoder choice. It isolates the effect of aggregation while leveraging the strong RNA encoder from config_031.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with transformer aggregation achieve strong performance (config_025: 0.713, config_031: 0.724). This experiment tests the impact of fusion method (concat vs weighted) for the same encoders, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It clarifies whether concat fusion could improve performance when using these encoders, balancing exploitation of strong components with exploration of critical design choices.
